FAST

MADRID: At least one crew member aboard a ship carrying diesel has died after the vessel capsized and partially sank off the Spanish island of Ibiza on Thursday (Nov 26), regional authorities said , adding there were no signs of pollution so far. The Malta-flagged chemical tanker Med Emre was sailing from Algeciras to Barcelona and may have been carrying up to 7,000 metric tons of diesel when it keeled over about 30 nautical miles (56 km) off Ibiza 's northwestern coast, the Balearic Islands' interior department said. Emergency services said all 17 crew members were rescued, but one died after being taken directly to Ibiza 's Can Misses hospital. Six others were brought to Ibiza airport and taken to two hospitals with light injuries, primarily hypothermia. Of the remaining crew, five were taken to Valencia and five remained in good condition aboard a rescue vessel, they added.

Pablo Garriz, the Balearic Islands' regional head of emergencies, said the crew included Turkish and Indian nationals, but he could not yet confirm the nationality of the deceased. The tanker remained partially submerged with its keel protruding above the surface, Garriz told reporters, despite initial indications that it had sunk completely. "The positive news is that the vessel is not on the seabed but remains semi-submerged at the surface, which allows salvage and containment operations," he said, adding there was currently no impact on Balearic waters or coastline and no evidence of a significant spill, although small sheens had been observed. Technical experts were assessing the vessel's stability before deciding on salvage and cargo-recovery operations, he added.

Spain's maritime rescue service sent an aircraft and a vessel specialised in oil-spill response, the Clara Campoamor, to survey the area. Three helicopters took part in the rescue, along with nearby merchant vessels. Spain's merchant marine authority activated the national maritime pollution contingency plan at level 2, the second-highest. The waters surrounding Ibiza are a habitat for sea turtles, dolphins and the Balearic shearwater, one of Europe's most threatened seabirds. The area is also home to extensive meadows of Posidonia oceanica seagrass, which plays a vital role in supporting marine biodiversity. Spain's worst maritime environmental disaster occurred in 2002, when the Bahamas-flagged tanker Prestige sank off the northwestern Galicia region, spilling tens of thousands of tons of heavy fuel oil and fouling hundreds of beaches in Spain and France. The Balearic regional government said it was gathering information on the accident and its possible consequences, including any risk of fuel pollution, before deciding on further measures.

Source: Reuters/fs

FAST

RIYADH: The Saudi - led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday (Nov 26) that the Iran-aligned group had attacked Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, a day after hitting the largest oil refinery in the kingdom. The refinery in the southwestern city of Jazan, near the Yemeni border, is designed to process up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day. The coalition said it had later destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in the Yemeni port city of Hodeidah, which it said the Houthis had used in Thursday's attack on the refinery. Earlier it said that targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure would be met with a firm military response.

On Wednesday the Houthis claimed attacks on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and a major crude export hub, and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan. The Saudi - led coalition said it had intercepted four drones over Ras Tanura and air defences had destroyed a drone near Jeddah Islamic Port. The Houthis , who control the most populous areas of Yemen including the capital Sanaa, have launched missiles and drones at Saudi airports, oil facilities and office buildings since Yemen's civil war reignited in July, in a spillover from the US-Iran war. The attacks have previously temporarily disrupted some of Aramco's operations and caused the cancellation of most international flights to Riyadh. They also forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including soccer's AFC Asian Cup and the flagship FII investment conference. Fighting has intensified since the Houthis seized strategic territory along Yemen's Red Sea coast in September and advanced towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital shipping route for Gulf oil producers seeking access to the Red Sea.

ROME: Two Italians were killed in a drone attack in Kuwait on Thursday (Nov 26) that Italy and Kuwait blamed on Iran, although Tehran has denied any involvement. The two were technicians working for Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian unit of German defence group Rheinmetall, and were at an air defence surveillance station in Kuwait when it was targeted by Iranian drones, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told the Senate in Rome. "Following a powerful explosion, both of our compatriots, according to information coming from Kuwait , have died. Two other people were injured: a Pakistani national and a captain in the Kuwait i army," Tajani said. Kuwait 's Defence Ministry confirmed that the two Italians had died of their injuries, after initially reporting that four people had been wounded by falling debris when a "vital facility" was targeted in what it said was an Iranian attack. It said the other two injured were Kuwait i and Pakistani nationals and that the attack had caused material damage.

Iran's senior Armed Forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi denied that Iran had attacked a "vital" site in Kuwait , saying no offensive or military operations by Iranian forces had taken place in the region, Iranian state media reported on Thursday. Iran's embassy in Rome also categorically denied the claims of an Iranian drone attack on a military site in Kuwait in a post on X. Tajani told Italian news agency AGI that Italy would lodge a complaint with the Iranian embassy over the incident, urging caution and saying there was no need to attack Arab countries bordering Iran that were not involved in the war. The regional conflict erupted on Feb 28 when the US and Israeli launched attacks on Iran, and it has since widened to include Iranian strikes on Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military bases. Earlier in November, Iran said it had targeted US drone and missile sites in Kuwait after the United States struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump says he asked Putin to 'pull back' military aggression throughout Europe

US President Donald Trump says he urged Russian leader Vladimir Putin to halt military aggression across Europe, language that appears to extend beyond Ukraine as concerns grow over alleged Russian actions elsewhere.

Russia's President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump shake hands during a meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders' Summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China, Nov 19, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Sputnik/Vyacheslav Prokofyev)

PALM BEACH, Florida: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday (Nov 26) he told Russian leader Vladimir Putin last week he would like to see Russia pull back on military aggression against territories throughout Europe in the hope it could lead to a quick settlement of the war in Ukraine. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe, in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post. "I really believe this is a strong possibility — Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH," Trump said. Trump has frequently urged a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine, but the phrase "territories throughout Europe" suggests territories beyond the battlefield in Ukraine.

Trump did not elaborate on what conduct he was asking Putin to halt. Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine started in 2022, other countries have occasionally accused Russia of provocative behaviour.

Related:

Trump and NATO chief urge Russia to avoid actions that widen Ukraine war

'Russia wants more than Ukraine,' says Germany's Merz as he defends aid for Kyiv

Trump did not elaborate on what conduct he was asking Putin to halt. Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine started in 2022, other countries have occasionally accused Russia of provocative behaviour. Later on Thursday, Trump reiterated his view that Putin wants to make a deal. But Trump, who has often regarded diplomacy as a matter of personal relationships, said animosity between the Russian leader and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made negotiations difficult. "The biggest problem to that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other," Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, where he was spending the Thanksgiving holiday. Trump said he did not know whether Putin would attend next month's G20 meeting in Florida and expressed doubts that the Russian leader would want to attend the Dec 14 to Dec 15 meeting. "If it were up to me, I'd like to have him," he said. The Kremlin said on Thursday that no decision had been made on Putin's participation in the summit. Poland, a NATO member, this week accused Russia of deliberately violating Polish airspace. Estonia recently linked an arson attack to Russia's military intelligence service.

Related:

Zelenskyy says Putin a 'killer' after Trump calls him his 'friend'

Commentary: Historic Xi-Trump-Putin summit reveals an unsettling truth about great power diplomacy

Trump met with Putin last week in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the APEC leaders' meeting, part of a diplomatic push by his administration to address the war in Ukraine and broader security issues. He also participated in a trilateral summit with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping . The Trump administration has argued that direct engagement with both leaders could help reduce global tensions, while critics have questioned whether Washington is applying sufficient pressure on Moscow to end the conflict. Trump's son-in-law and diplomatic envoy Jared Kushner on Wednesday praised Putin as a "grandmaster of politics" and a "historic figure" in a podcast interview with Mathias Dopfner, chief executive of German media group Axel Springer. Kushner argued that Putin had shown "restraint" by refraining from using nuclear weapons despite the risk of the Ukraine war escalating dramatically, and that he believed Putin wanted peace and improved relations with the United States.

Trump demands probe of GDP data released before midterms

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday (Nov 26) demanded an immediate probe into what he alleged was a deliberate decision to release "fake" growth numbers before this month's midterm elections . The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis on Wednesday revised third-quarter annualised growth up to 4.3 per cent from the advance estimate of 3.4 per cent it announced on Oct 29. Trump 's Republican Party suffered heavy losses in the Nov 3 election. "It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE," Trump said in a Truth Social post, without providing evidence. "Why wasn't the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation. This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error," he said. The BEA has previously said that its estimates can differ from the final numbers because advance estimates for quarterly growth lack complete source data on inventories, trade, and consumer spending on services. Last year, Trump fired a top Labour Department official, accusing her without evidence of manipulating the figures and adding to already growing concerns about the quality of economic data published by the federal government.
